title: POC calendar, gates & benchmark playbook — Venturi AI
summary: Kickoff to align on measurable POC gates: define success criteria (latency, accuracy, cost), agree workload slices for benchmarks, set access dates for VPC/Dedicated test cluster, pick midpoint check-in metrics, and schedule executive readout. Action items include security questionnaire, sample dataset delivery, and benchmark script handoff.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Venturi Head ML), Samir (Platform), Ellen (Security), Carlos (Product)

00:00 - Maya: Okay, thanks everyone for jumping on. Uh this is the kickoff for the Venturi POC — our aim is to map out timeline, success gates and exactly what we'll benchmark. We have Diego from the eng side to cover infra questions.
00:28 - Priya: Hi all. Thanks. Quick note — timeline is tight for us, we want an exec readout in five weeks if possible.
00:44 - Diego: Cool, good to know. We'll need to size the workload first — Samir, can you describe your expected traffic patterns?
01:10 - Samir: Sure. For the first POC slice we expect bursty consumer traffic — roughly 60 rps at peak for short chat-style queries, median prompt length ~60 tokens, some longer inference up to 2k tokens but rare. Also a small batch job for nightly embeddings for search, ~10k docs.
01:36 - Maya: Great — so two workload types: interactive low-latency and batch embeddings. That informs recommended instance types and whether Dedicated makes sense vs hosted.
01:55 - Ellen: From security we need clarity on data residency, KMS integration, and audit logs. We operate under SOC2-like internal controls and we'd need HSM or customer-managed keys.
02:18 - Diego: We support KMS integrations in Private, and Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS via our API. For hosted we offer encryption at rest but not customer-managed HSM by default — could be a blocker.
02:42 - Priya: Ok that may push us to Dedicated or Private. For the POC can we get a short checklist of what's required for VPC peering and service account creation?
03:03 - Maya: Yes, we'll send a network prerequisites doc. Action: Maya to share a checklist.
03:18 - Carlos: On success criteria, leadership wants three clear metrics: p95 latency < 300ms for interactive, embedding throughput >= 8 docs/sec for the nightly job, and cost per 1M tokens below our current baseline by at least 15%. Accuracy/regression is also a gate — we'll provide a gold set for quality checks.
03:46 - Diego: That's helpful. For latency we should specify sequence lengths used in p95. If median is 60 tokens but p95 includes longer sessions we need a distribution.
04:03 - Samir: We'll export a traffic histogram from production — expect to have that by Tuesday.
04:18 - Maya: Timeline proposal: Week 0 (this week) — access & network setup. Week 1 — baseline runs and small scale benchmarks. Week 2–3 — full workload benchmarks and tuning. Week 4 — midpoint readout (internal). Week 5 — exec readout. Does that align with five-week ask?
04:40 - Priya: Yes but we need mid-point to include a live demo for an exec; otherwise they won't see progress.
04:52 - Diego: We can plan a short demo at midpoint, but we recommend checkpoint metrics rather than full polished UX.
05:10 - Ellen: Also need to confirm retention/ingestion: logs for the POC should be disabled or redacted — we don't want PII leaving environment. What are Redwood's defaults?
05:27 - Diego: By default, no customer prompts are stored for hosted, but Dedicated/Private are under customer control. We'll produce a config template to disable logging.
05:42 - Maya: I'll include that in the checklist.
06:00 - Carlos: Benchmarks — what exact scripts do you run? We want reproducibility so we can re-run on our infra later.
06:18 - Diego: We use a benchmark harness (open-source style) that accepts open formats — request JSONs, sequence length distribution, concurrency. We'll share the harness and a runbook. It includes KPIs: latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95), throughput, tokens/sec, and cost-per-token calculation.
06:45 - Priya: For quality/regression we'll need model-output diffs on our labeled prompts. Can Redwood run A/B comparisons between model variants?
07:02 - Diego: Yes, we can pin model versions and do canary vs baseline runs. Note: variants sometimes have different quantization; results may vary.
07:22 - Maya: On the billing side for Dedicated POC we typically provide short-term credits; we'll include pricing scenarios: hosted (pay-as-you-go), dedicated reserved trial, and private evaluation.
07:39 - Samir: Cost is a big factor. If we go Dedicated we need clear estimate per 1M tokens for our workload mix.
07:55 - Diego: We'll run the baseline with your histogram and give a cost projection. Expect a first pass within 3 business days after we get the traffic sample.
08:12 - Priya: Access timing — can we get network access in 48 hours? We need to provision service accounts and firewall rules.
08:26 - Maya: We'll try. Depends on your security review outcome. Ellen, can you share the security questionnaire answers by EOD Monday?
08:38 - Ellen: I'll try, but we may need clarifications.
08:46 - Maya: Noted — Maya to send questionnaire link and schedule an optional security sync.
09:00 - Carlos: Midpoint readout: what artifacts will we present? Want a one-pager with numbers and a demo clip.
09:12 - Diego: We'll deliver a benchmark report (CSV + charts), configuration snapshot, and a short demo script.
09:28 - Priya: Also please include failure cases and suggested optimizations — especially around KV cache sizing and batching tunables.
09:44 - Diego: Agreed — we'll surface cache hit rates and effective batching metrics. I should flag that 'KV cache' sometimes got transcribed as 'KV cash' in our internal notes, so sorry for that past confusion.
10:02 - Maya: Good callout.
10:10 - Samir: A question about embeddings: our nightly job currently runs on CPU cluster and takes ~2h. If Redwood can do embeddings faster, what's the API? Batch upload?
10:26 - Diego: We support bulk embedding endpoints and streaming for large sets. For bulk we'll ask for a manifest file and support resumable uploads.
10:40 - Priya: For the exec readout, our VP expects an ROI estimate — can Redwood help with projected cost delta?
10:54 - Maya: Yes we'll produce a short ROI slide showing cost delta and latency improvements vs current baseline.
11:06 - Carlos: What about model choice: we initially want to evaluate two open models and a Redwood-optimized variant. Will that complicate the benchmark?
11:20 - Diego: It's fine; we recommend running the same harness across variants. Note that quantized variants may change accuracy slightly — include regen checks.
11:40 - Priya: Any constraints on sequence length for the dedicated infra? We might test 2k token contexts for a subset.
11:55 - Diego: Dedicated supports long context but performance will be model & kernel dependent. We'll include a long-context run in the full workload phase.
12:12 - Maya: Ok final recap and next steps: 1) Maya send network & security checklist + benchmark harness link (today). 2) Venturi to send traffic histogram & sample dataset (by Tue). 3) Diego to run baseline and share cost projection (within 3 business days of sample). 4) Security sync if needed (Ellen open). 5) Midpoint demo scheduled for Week 4 and exec readout Week 5.
12:53 - Priya: Sounds good. Quick Q — who owns the runbook updates after the POC?
13:05 - Maya: We'll hand off runbook to Venturi but Redwood will keep a living doc until production handoff.
13:15 - Ellen: One more note — will you sign an NDA for the sample dataset?
13:25 - Maya: Yes, we can accelerate an NDA. I'll attach to the checklist.
13:40 - Carlos: Great, thanks everyone.
13:47 - Maya: Thanks team, we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling invites.
14:00 - End of meeting.

Notes: occasional stutters and mislabeled speakers — e.g., a few sections show 'Speaker 2' in the recording but context clarified names. There were short cross-talks and filler words. Some product names in the recording were transcribed as Redwood "Opti-mize" or "Dedicated" spelled out incorrectly.

Venturi to provide traffic histogram and sample dataset (by 2026-07-13)
